title: Evidence Curation Orchestrator — spec & runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This document defines the Evidence Curation Orchestrator (ECO) — a lightweight operator that aggregates, enriches, and routes control evidence (audit events, RBAC decision logs, control-state snapshots) into downstream stores and SIEMs. ECO's aim: reliable, observable delivery with minimal transformation surface so downstream forensics and compliance tooling can operate deterministically.

Scope: (what ECO does)
- Ingests canonical audit event stream (primary source: runtime audit bus, secondary sources: service write-aheads).
- Applies canonical mapping to Audit Schema v2 (flat key/value envelope).
- Enriches events with RBAC-v2 decision metadata, tenant labels, and request trace ids.
- Samples and annotates long-lived binaries/attachments (evidence blobs) and routes them to long-term archive with pointers in the event envelope.
- Batches and exports to multiple sinks (Splunk HEC, Elastic Bulk, QRadar syslog, internal Evidence Lake).
- Maintains per-event delivery state, idempotency, and TTL-driven rotation.
- Exposes health, lag, and per-sink backpressure signals to Console.

Non-goals:
- No heavy reformatting (avoid changing semantics of events).
- Not an ingestion-level schema validator (basic checks only).
- Not a replacement for forensic chain-of-custody service — will emit proof-hashes and handoff tokens.

Design goals / success criteria:
- Once-and-only-once semantics to SIEMs within operational bounds (best-effort for third-party sinks; at-least-once with strong dedupe keys where exact once isn't supported).
- Low tail latency for high-priority control events (security alerts).
- Deterministic export format across deployments (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).
- Configurable routing rules by customer, team, and control type.
- Clear operational metrics: in-flight, retry queue size, per-sink ack latency, failed-to-archive ratio.

High-level architecture:
- Input adapters: pulls from audit pub/sub (primary), optionally from event store snapshot files for backfill.
- Normalizer: minimal transform to canonical event envelope.
- Enricher: RBAC lookup service, tenant metadata cache, sample TTL manager.
- Curation engine: batching, dedupe key generation, sign/attach proof-hash, per-sink routing policy, persistent delivery queue.
- Sink adapters: Splunk HEC client, Elastic Bulk client, Syslog/TCP client, S3/Archive client for blobs.
- Observability: Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, distributed traces, per-event tracing id.

Canonical event envelope (flat JSON - exported):
- Note: keep envelope flat, no nested objects except small arrays (tags). Avoid nested objects to simplify SIEM mapping.

Sample exported event (stringified JSON that will be sent to sinks):
{
  "event_id": "e-20241115-000012345",
  "occurred_at": "2024-11-15T14:21:03.123Z",
  "service": "auth-service",
  "host": "auth-prod-12",
  "tenant_id": "acct-7b4f2",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "actor_id": "u-89a2",
  "rbac_decision": "DENY",
  "rbac_policy_id": "rbac-v2::policy-34",
  "resource_type": "model-endpoint",
  "resource_id": "endpoint-nt-23",
  "action": "invoke",
  "request_id": "r-33f1",
  "trace_id": "trace-abcdef123456",
  "outcome": "403",
  "decision_latency_ms": "12",
  "attachments": "s3://evidence-archive/2024/11/e-20241115-000012345-meta.json",
  "proof_sha256": "sha256:8c7f...",
  "export_dest": "splunk-hec://us-1",
  "route_version": "v1",
  "tags": "security,rbac,high-priority"
}

Key mapping and normalization rules (short):
- All timestamps must be ISO-8601 and normalized to UTC. Field name: occurred_at.
- Numeric fields must be strings for SIEM compatibility where required (decision_latency_ms as string).
- actor_id/tenant_id/resource_id must be opaque ids with prefix to avoid collisions.
- attachments: a single string pointer if any blob exists. Multiple blobs should be concatenated with `;` or stored in archive manifest (avoid nested arrays).

Export contracts (sink specifics):
- Splunk HEC: send as event payload, include X-Redwood-Route header for routing, HEC must be idempotent with dedupe key header X-Idempotency-Key = event_id. Retry window 48h.
- Elastic Bulk: use index `evidence-YYYY.MM.DD`, document id = event_id. On version conflict, log and drop (primary index is authoritative).
- QRadar/syslog: flatten and send as RFC5424 KV pairs, include proof_sha256 in msg. Max message size 64 KB; if exceeds, route attachment to archive and send pointer only.

Delivery semantics and idempotency:
- Primary persistence: internal delivery queue (durable DB, per-tenant namespace).
- Dedupe key: event_id + route_version. Sinks that support dedupe: Elastic (doc id), Splunk (idempotency header). If sink can't dedupe, ECO will keep small local watermark for 72h to avoid double-send for retries.
- Retries: exponential backoff with jitter, max retry window configurable per sink (default 48h). After max retries, event enters dead-letter queue and alerting runs.

Batching and backpressure rules:
- Batch size target: 512 events or 128 KB per batch, whichever first.
- High-priority routes (security alerts) bypass batching and go immediate (single-event flush).
- Backpressure: if sink latency > 2x SLO for 3 consecutive periods, reduce batch size and prioritize immediate small batches. If queues > threshold, circuit-break to secondary sink if configured.

Attachment / blob handling:
- Blobs ingested to Archive service S3-compatible with stable object keys. ECO writes manifest record to event.attachments.
- Blobs are TTL-tagged; ECO enforces two-phase retention labels: short-term (90d) and long-term (3650d) with legal-hold override.
- Proof-of-custody: ECO computes sha256 over canonical blob bytes and stores proof_sha256 on event and in archive metadata.

RBAC-v2 enrichment pattern:
- At ingest, ECO calls RBAC Decision Cache (local LRU with TTL 30s) with (actor, resource, action). Returns policy id, evaluated rules, and decision_latency_ms. Record minimal fields in envelope to avoid PII.
- If RBAC service unavailable, tag event with rbac_deadman=true and route to higher-fidelity archival path.

Observability and telemetry (to Console):
- Metrics per tenant: events_ingested_total, events_exported_total{sink}, events_failed_total{reason}, avg_export_latency_ms, queue_depth, deadletter_size.
- Dashboards: per-tenant lag (seconds), per-sink retry rate, top N failing event reasons.
- Traces: attach trace_id to all spans.

Operational runbook (short):
- S1: Splunk HEC 5xx spikes -> examine splunk ack latency > 30s, scale ECO worker pool, if sustained, switch to secondary endpoint and open incident.
- S2: Archive upload failure -> retry queue, if object store ACLs changed, fail fast and alert security.
- S3: Duplicates visible in Elastic (doc version conflict) -> check dedupe watermark and routes, escalate if >0.1% of daily events.

Migration notes from current collector: 
- Provide adapter that mimics existing collector topic format for 4 weeks. Run ECO in parallel (shadow) and compare exported counts and proof_sha256 between systems (route_version=v2).
- Backfill strategy: rehydrate events from primary event store and replay through ECO with backfill flag; mark backfill=true in envelope.

Security considerations:
- All inter-service traffic TLS mutual auth.
- Minimal PII in envelope; sensitive fields must be redacted and only included as attachments with controlled access.
- KMS-signed manifests for legal-hold operations.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- SLA for dead-letter TTL before auto-delete? (propose 90d default)
- Legal hold operational workflow — manual override in Console vs API-only?
- Should ECO perform full JSON schema validation and reject vs accept-with-warnings?

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- (Ethan) prototype Splunk HEC adapter with idempotency header (due 2024-11-30).
- (Sofia) RBAC-v2 cache API contract review and QoS guarantees (due 2024-12-04).
- (Aisha) draft console wiring for per-tenant routing rules (due 2024-12-10).
- Create SEC-410 JIRA epic for implementation and SEC-411/412 tasks for sink adapters.

Appendix: quick config example (YAML style as text)
---
route_rules:
  - name: security-alerts
    match: "tags contains 'security' or outcome startswith '5'"
    priority: 10
    sinks: ["splunk-us-primary","archive"]
    batching: {max_events: 1, max_bytes: 8192}
  - name: default-audit
    match: "true"
    priority: 1
    sinks: ["elastic-main"]
    batching: {max_events: 512, max_bytes: 131072}

Implementation checklist (short):
- [ ] adapter: audit pubsub input
- [ ] normalizer + schema tests
- [ ] enricher: RBAC cache integration
- [ ] archive client: put/get + proof metadata
- [ ] sink adapters: Splunk, Elastic, Syslog
- [ ] delivery queue + persistent watermark store
- [ ] Console pages: per-tenant routing, dead-letter explorer
- [ ] chaos test plan and perf benchmark (1M events/day tenant sample)

Notes to self: avoid over-normalizing — downstream forensics rely on original field semantics. Keep ECO as a "curator" not a translator.
